title: Femtosecond Laser Implantation of a 355-Degree Intrastromal Corneal Ring Segment in Keratoconus: A Three-Year Follow-Up

groups.description: 38 eyes of 26 patients (18-38 years) with central moderate or severe keratoconus receiving a 355-degree Keraring through a femtosecond laser tunnel; prospective interventional case series (Methods, Table 1)

exclusions.reason: means include eyes whose ring extruded and was explanted (a second procedure) inside the primary-treatment group: Table 6 and the Discussion report extrusions from 12 months on, followed by explantation and progression

notes: Ring extrusion (Table 6) is counted at 12, 24 and 36 months and ended in explantation in about a third of eyes by 36 months; the Discussion says most corneal melting began after 6 months. The article does not state that no ring was removed before 6 months.
Age group mixed: Table 1 gives an age range of 18-38 years (the inclusion criterion says older than 20 years); 18-year-olds count as paediatric under the protocol.
Moderate (16 eyes) and severe (22 eyes) stages are not tabulated separately for Kmax; the whole cohort is extracted.
K min and K mean (Table 4), visual acuity (Table 2), refraction (Table 3) and efficacy and safety indices (Table 5) are tabulated and not used.

series.notes: mean ± SD rows; Pentacam Scheimpflug imaging (Methods); the table gives no unit, dioptres from the Results (K max <= 52 D staging) and the Table 2 footnote; per-visit n not reported
